newsitem.title: UK: Rowland blasts Lonrho stake sale to Anglo.
newsitem.headline: Rowland blasts Lonrho stake sale to Anglo.

text.p: Tiny Rowland, Lonrho's founder, on Wednesday sharply criticised the sale by chief executive Dieter Bock of an 18.3 percent stake in the conglomerate to South Africa's Anglo American.
"It is fine for Anglo, but it's not fine for Lonrho shareholders," said Rowland, who was deposed from Lonrho's board in March 1995.
Rowland said Anglo American was known for the poor performance of its subsidiaries.
"I am not positive on the yield of Anglo's companies," the controversial businessman told Reuters in an interview.
"There are plenty of analysts to tell you what the returns are of Anglo's companies," said Rowland, who founded Lonrho 34 years ago.
Anglo American now holds a 25.9 percent stake in Lonrho, which is about to be broken into three parts.
Lonrho on Wednesday announced it was about to complete the sale of its hotels, which is to be followed by the divestment of its African trading arm.
The remaining Lonrho rump would consist of the mining operations, with which Anglo American wants to co-operate. The South African firm, however said it does not intend to make an offer for Lonrho.
